newsitem.title: USA: McKesson to buy General Medical for $775 million.
newsitem.headline: McKesson to buy General Medical for $775 million.

text.p: McKesson Corp. said Tuesday it agreed to acquire General Medical Inc., a privately held supplier of health care supplies, in a deal valued at $775 million, including the assumption of debt.
The combined company will be the largest health care supply management company in North America, it said.
General Medical supplies medical products to the full range of alternate-site health care facilities, including doctors and clinics, long-term care and home-care sites.

McKesson, a supplier of wholesale pharmaceuticals and related services, hopes the purchase will give it a stronger presence in the alternate-site medical market, the fastest growing sector for drugs and medical supplies.
The company will pay $347 million -- half in McKesson common stock and half in cash -- for the equity of General Medical. It also will assume $428 million in debt.

McKesson, based in San Francisco, said it will issue 2.75 million to 3.72 million shares in the deal, depending on the price of its stock just before the deal closes. McKesson rose 62.5 cents to $55.50 late on the New York Stock Exchange.
General Medical will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of McKesson, retaining its current senior management team.

"The combination of McKesson and General Medical will create a strong new force for shaping the health care supply needs of physicians, extended-care facilities, and integrated health care networks," McKesson Chairman Alan Seelenfreund said in a statement.
McKesson said it expects the acquisition to boost earnings in the first year after the deal closes within two months, subject to regulatory approvals.
General Medical distrubutes more than 130,000 products to more than 200,000 care providers. It had 1996 revenues of about $1.7 billion.
